lines.trans: Lift the left side half a centimetre, Rami—now drop it onto the pin!
Solid! Swing it open against the stone wall and hook the iron catch.
Stand back by the courtyard tree, Nour. How does the colour look in daylight?
Like the room belonged to the tree all along! Green shutters, white arches, warm stone!
Now let us carry twelve folded chairs inside and wipe down the four cellar tables.
I measured the floor plan: four tables inside Room Nine, four outside under the lanterns.
And if it drizzles on Wednesday, twelve guests can still sit warm and dry behind the glass!
Look who is peering down from the upstairs landing—Mazen is beaming!
No green paint on his glasses today either!
All heavy work is finished twenty hours early, Nour.
Now I only need to write clean café signs and help Salma in the kitchen!
Don't celebrate yet—check the kitchen first. Salma has six trays of lemons out.

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine بيضا (beida) and plural بيض (biid).

examples.trans: We brought clean white sheets.
The gift is wrapped in white paper.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خضرا, plural: خضر).

examples.trans: Pass beside the green pharmacy.
Put the green herbs on the eggs.

meanings.note: Numeral 'four'; short form أربع (arba') directly before a plural noun (أربع طاولات 'four tables').

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.
Four tables and eight chairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Everyday conditional word 'if' for real possibilities.

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

examples.text: إذا فتحنا الساحة الصبح، الجيران بيفرحوا.
examples.trans: If we open the courtyard in the morning, the neighbours will be delighted.

meanings.note: Form VIII verb taking بـ for what is celebrated.

examples.text: رح نحتفل بافتتاح الكافيه مع كل الجيران.
examples.trans: We're going to celebrate the café opening with all the neighbours.

examples.text: احتفلنا لما خلص دهان الشيش قبل المغرب.
examples.trans: We celebrated when the shutter painting finished before dusk.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'twelve'; before a singular counted noun it takes -r: اطنعشر دقة ('twelve chimes').

examples.trans: The clock tower chimed twelve!
Here is twelve dinars change.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The guest arrived Wednesday night.
We meet on Wednesday morning.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('outside the gate') and standalone ('outside').

examples.trans: It is raining outside.
A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بسطات.

examples.trans: Turn left at the stair landing.
The landing is wide and bright.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'early'.

examples.trans: You arrived ten minutes early.
We wake up early every day.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('under, beneath') and standalone ('downstairs').

examples.trans: Let us bring it downstairs into the light.
The wide desk is under the window.

meanings.note: Numeral 'nine'; short form تسع (tisa') before a plural noun (تسع دقايق 'nine minutes').

examples.trans: The quietness in the courtyard is nine out of ten!
She came back in just nine minutes!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تقيلة, plural: تقال).

examples.trans: This suitcase is very heavy today.
Take off your heavy coat and sit down to rest.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بثبت, بيثبت).

examples.trans: Hold still a moment and listen to that sound!

examples.text: الكرسي ثبت بعد ما شدينا البرغي.
examples.trans: The chair held firm once we tightened the screw.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أجزاء.

examples.trans: This is the sweetest part of the story.
I read the first part of the book.

meanings.note: Verbal/abstract noun from جف ('become dry').

examples.text: الخشب بالبيانو بيحب جو معتدل ومش رطوبة شديدة.
examples.trans: Piano wood likes moderate air rather than extreme dampness or dryness.

examples.text: جفاف الهوا بعمان بيساعد الدهان ينشف بسرعة.
examples.trans: The dryness of Amman's air helps the paint dry fast.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'next to, beside'.

examples.trans: Put a napkin beside every cup.
There is no light beside the bed.

meanings.note: Used with right and left: الجهة اليمين 'the right side', من هاي الجهة 'from this side'.

examples.trans: The kitchen is on the other side.
Walk this way, it is closer.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('inside the bag') and standalone ('inside').

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
The water is flowing inside!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: حجار.

examples.trans: Old stone holds warmth.
She stepped onto the stone step outside.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The iron gate is locked at night.
Pass me the heavy iron wrench.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: حيطان.

examples.trans: We hung the mirror on the wall.
Stone walls keep the coolness in summer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خفيفة, plural: خفاف).

examples.trans: Coffee with milk and light sugar.
A light, tasty breakfast in the morning.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

خِلِص.gloss: to run out; be finished; end

meanings.en: to run out; be finished; end
meanings.note: Form I intransitive counterpart of transitive خلّص ('to finish something'): خلص الخبز means 'the bread has run out'.

examples.text: يلا نمشي قبل ما يخلص الخبز السخن.
examples.trans: Let's walk over before the hot bread sells out.

examples.text: خلصت القهوة، رح أعمل إبريق جديد.
examples.trans: The coffee ran out; I will make a fresh pot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: دافية, plural: دافيين).

examples.trans: The bread is warm and fresh from the oven.
Sitting in the attic is cozy when it rains.

meanings.note: Unvocalised درج covers both daraj ('stairs', masculine collective) and durj ('desk drawer').

examples.trans: Go up the stairs to the second floor.
The big notebook is inside the drawer.

meanings.note: Single hinged panel or leaf of a double window, shutter, or cupboard.

examples.text: فتحنا الدرفة الشمال وبعدين الدرفة اليمين.
examples.trans: We swung open the left shutter leaf and then the right one.

examples.text: كل شباك إله درفتين خشب متينات.
examples.trans: Each window has two sturdy wooden shutter panels.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Old stone holds warmth at night.
Morning warmth from the sun is comforting.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دهانات.

examples.trans: Room eight has fresh paint.

examples.text: ريحة الدهان راحت لما فتحنا الشباك.
examples.trans: The smell of paint cleared when we opened the window.

meanings.note: Warm everyday Jordanian word for 'ear', especially in idioms like الضحكة من الذان للذان ('grinning ear to ear').

examples.text: مازن كان مبتسم والضحكة من الذان للذان.
examples.trans: Mazen was smiling from ear to ear.

examples.text: همس الكلمة بذاني عشان ما يسمع الباقي.
examples.trans: He whispered the word in my ear so the others wouldn't hear.

رجع.gloss: to return; come back; start again

meanings.en: to return; come back; start again
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برجع, بيرجع).

examples.trans: Can you run there and come back in ten minutes?
Did the pipe start dripping again?

meanings.note: Geminate verb used for splashing water or sprinkling herbs/sugar.

examples.trans: I sprinkled a little water on the flowers in the morning.

examples.text: سلمى رشت قرفة مطحونة فوق الكيكة.
examples.trans: Salma dusted ground cinnamon over the cake.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برفع, بيرفع).

examples.trans: Lift the handle first and then push.
He raised his cup in a toast to the neighbours.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساعات.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بساعد, بيساعد).

examples.trans: He will surely love to help us!
We helped the guest carry her suitcase.

meanings.note: Numeral 'six'; short form ست (sitt) before a plural noun (ست سنين 'six years').

examples.trans: Room six is on the second floor.
I have six lemons in the basket.

meanings.note: Shortened in speech to سنتي (dual سنتيين 'two centimetres').

examples.text: قيس المسافة بالمسطرة، لازم تكون عشرة سنتي.
examples.trans: Measure the gap with the ruler—it has to be ten centimetres.

examples.text: كم قميصك بعيد سنتيين بس عن الدهان الرطب!
examples.trans: Your shirt sleeve is only two centimetres from the wet paint!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Singulative noun ('one tree') of collective شجر ('trees').

examples.text: قطفنا ليمون أصفر طازة من شجرة الساحة.
examples.trans: We picked fresh yellow lemons from the courtyard tree.

examples.text: ظل الشجرة بيبرد القعدة وقت الظهر.
examples.trans: The shade of the tree cools the seating area at noon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أشغال.

examples.text: حبيت الشغل هون من أول يوم.
examples.trans: I loved the work here from day one.
Let us finish our work before noon.

meanings.note: In everyday Jordanian directions, شمال (shmaal) means 'left' (contrast شَمال shamaal 'north').

examples.trans: Turn left at the street corner.
The key is on the shelf to your left.

meanings.note: Broken plural صواني ('serving trays' or 'oven baking pans').

examples.text: جهزنا تلات صواني خبز عشان تدخل الفرن الفجر.
examples.trans: We prepped three trays of bread to go into the oven at dawn.

examples.text: نور حملت صينية الشاي بالنعنع للساحة.
examples.trans: Nour carried the mint tea tray out to the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بضل, بيضل).

examples.trans: Family is what remains.
My teacup stayed intact inside the suitcase!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ضيوف.

examples.trans: The guests are coming down to breakfast now.
We welcomed every guest with a smile.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: طاولات.

examples.trans: We set four tables in the courtyard.
Breakfast is ready on the table.

طلع.gloss: to go up; go out; come out; turn out

meanings.en: to go up; go out; come out; turn out
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطلع, بيطلع).

examples.text: لفائف القرفة هلا طلعت من الفرن!
examples.trans: The cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven!
Go up the stairs to the third floor.

meanings.note: Before a time noun, طول (tuul) means 'all ... long / throughout' (طول الليل all night long, طول الأسبوع all week).

examples.trans: The rain fell all night long.
Breakfast is free all week long.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطل, بيطل).

examples.text: مازن بيطل من ورا الستارة كل دقيقة!
examples.trans: Mazen peeks from behind the curtain every minute!
The window overlooks the courtyard and the tree.

meanings.note: Numeral 'twenty' (followed by a singular noun in Arabic: عشرين دقيقة 'twenty minutes').

examples.trans: We need twenty eggs for breakfast.
The ring's width is twenty millimetres.

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: Arabic expresses age with عمر + possessive suffix: عمره تمانين سنة ('its/his age is eighty years').

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
He has lived in this quarter all his life.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: غرف.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: فوانيس.

examples.trans: The golden lanterns are lit in the courtyard.
We hung a brass lantern by the entrance.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفتح, بيفتح).

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
Oh, the door finally opened!

meanings.note: Form II causative of فات ('enter'): 'carry/bring inside'.

examples.text: تعالوا نفوت الطاولات الخشب قبل ما تشتي.
examples.trans: Come help us carry the wooden tables inside before it rains.

examples.text: فوتنا درفات الشيش عالممر عشان تنشف.
examples.trans: We brought the shutter panels into the hallway to dry.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('above, over') and standalone ('upstairs').

examples.trans: The window is above the old tree.
Let us go upstairs to see the room.

في.gloss: there is; there are; is there?

meanings.en: there is; there are; is there?
meanings.note: Spoken Levantine existential word ('there is / there are'); negated as ما في ('there is no / there are no').

examples.trans: There is a small paper tag on the handle.
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقيس, بيقيس).

examples.trans: I measure quietness and acoustics in courtyards.
The shopkeeper measured it against the old valve.

meanings.note: Means 'before' (قبل الفطور) and with a time span 'ago' (قبل ساعة 'an hour ago', قبل شوي 'just now').

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أقبية.

examples.trans: The boiler is down in the basement.
He went down to the cellar to get the toolbox.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقدر, بيقدر).

examples.text: بنقدر نقدم زبدة مالحة مع المربى؟
examples.trans: Can we serve salted butter with jam?

examples.text: ليش ما قدرت تعطيه القطار بإيدك؟
examples.trans: Why could you not hand him the train yourself?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قريبة, plural: قراب).

examples.text: علمت بيانو ببيت قريب من هون.
examples.trans: I taught piano in a house near here.
We booked a table at a nearby restaurant.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of زجاج ('glass').

examples.trans: Look at the courtyard through the window glass.
We wiped the glass this morning until it shone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقعد, بيقعد).

examples.trans: Please have a seat in the courtyard under the tree.

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay the whole week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أقواس.

examples.text: ادخل عالساحة من هاد القوس الحجري.
examples.trans: Step into the courtyard through this stone arch.

examples.text: الأقواس القديمة مبنية من حجر عمان.
examples.trans: The old arches are built of Amman limestone.

meanings.note: Introduces a vivid comparison ('as if / just like'); takes pronoun suffixes or stands as كأن before nouns.

examples.text: الخشب الأخضر والليمون الأصفر كأنهم جنينة حقيقية.
examples.trans: The green wood and yellow lemons look just like a real garden.

examples.text: البيانو بعد الدوزان صار يرن كأنه جديد.
examples.trans: After tuning, the piano rings out as if it were brand new.

meanings.note: Arabic uses no 'is/are' in the simple present, while كان supplies the past ('was/were') and يكون / بيكون supplies future or modal 'be'.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day will not be boring!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بكتب, بيكتب).

examples.text: رح يكتب تقييم حلو عن النزل.
examples.trans: He will write a lovely review of the guesthouse.
I wrote my name and number on the card.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: كراسي.

examples.trans: We placed eight chairs around the tables.
I tightened the screw on the wooden chair.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite singular noun كل means 'every' (كل يوم 'every day'); before a definite noun it means 'all / the whole' (كل الأسبوع 'all week').

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

كمان.gloss: also; too; again (كمان مرة once more)

meanings.en: also; too; again (كمان مرة once more)
meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for 'also, too, more' (كمان مرة 'one more time / again').

examples.text: التفكير السريع أنقذ الفطور كمان مرة!
examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast once again!
And I missed you too.

meanings.note: Question word 'how?'.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?
Tell me how to find the shop.

meanings.note: Standalone لا means 'no'; before a 2nd-person subjunctive verb it forms a negative command (لا تقلقي 'do not worry!'), and لا ... ولا means 'neither ... nor'.

examples.trans: No, lift the handle first.
Do not worry, ma'am.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لوحات.

examples.text: شوف لوحة المفاتيح الخشب ورا المكتب.
examples.trans: Look at the wooden key board behind the desk.
We wiped the dust off the brass plate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ألوان.

examples.trans: The colour of the suitcase is dark blue.
The courtyard colours are soothing to the eye.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ليمون.

examples.trans: The warm lemon cake is ready.
I squeezed half a lemon into the soup.

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Classic Jordanian/Levantine craftsmanship word for a solid joint, wall, or hinge.

examples.text: ركبنا الشيش ببراغي طويلة فطلعت الدرفة ماكنة.
examples.trans: We mounted the shutters with long screws so the panel came out sturdy.

examples.text: الكرسي الخشب ماكن وبيتحمل شغل الساحة يوميا.
examples.trans: The wooden chair is solid and handles daily courtyard use.

meanings.note: Active participle of ابتسم ('to smile').

examples.text: أبو طارق وقف بنص الساحة مبتسم ومبسوط.
examples.trans: Abu Tariq stood in the middle of the courtyard smiling happily.

examples.text: نور بتستقبل الضيوف الصبح بوجه بشوش ومبتسم.
examples.trans: Nour greets guests in the morning with a warm, smiling face.

meanings.note: Used for architectural/room floor plans, schedules, and blueprints.

examples.text: رسمنا المخطط الجديد للطاولات بملف الاستقبال.
examples.trans: We drew the new table floor plan in the front-desk folder.

examples.text: حسب المخطط في مكان مريح لست طاولات بالساحة.
examples.trans: According to the layout there is comfortable room for six tables in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مرتبة, plural: مرتبين).

examples.trans: I recognized your neat handwriting right away.
Neat pencil sketches.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بمسح, بيمسح).

examples.trans: Wipe the dust off the brass plate.
We wiped down the tables before breakfast.

meanings.note: General word for a metal nail, peg, or tuning pin inside a piano.

examples.text: ركبت المفتاح بحذر على مسمار الدوزان التاني.
examples.trans: I fitted the wrench carefully onto the second tuning pin.

examples.text: دقينا مسمارين صغار عشان نعلق لوحة البوابة.
examples.trans: We tapped in two small nails to hang the gate sign.

meanings.note: Instrumental noun from شبك ('fasten/clip'): names a shutter catch/hook or paper clip.

examples.text: ثبتنا الشيش عالحيط بمشبك حديد أسود ماكن.
examples.trans: We secured the shutter against the wall with a sturdy black iron catch.

examples.text: تأكد إن المشبك مسكر منيح قبل ما تهب الريح.
examples.trans: Make sure the catch is latched tightly before the wind blows.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مطابخ.

examples.trans: The smell of bread is coming from the kitchen.
The guesthouse kitchen is spacious and clean.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أمطار.

examples.trans: Please come inside out of the cold rain.
The trees are green and lovely after the rain.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مطوية, plural: مطويين).

examples.trans: We found an old folded map in the box.

examples.text: في ورقة تانية مطوية ورا الإشعار.
examples.trans: There is a second folded sheet behind the notice.

meanings.note: Formal/signboard Arabic word for 'café' (alongside conversational كافيه), ideal for painted signs.

examples.text: كتبنا عاللوحة: مقهى جنينة الغرفة تسعة.
examples.trans: We painted on the sign: Room Nine Garden Café.

examples.text: المقهى رح يفتح يوميا من الصبح للمسا.
examples.trans: The café will be open daily from morning till evening.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مواعيد.

examples.trans: I always appreciate punctuality.

examples.text: عندنا موعد مهم يوم الجمعة الظهر.
examples.trans: We have an important appointment Friday at noon.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian question word for 'who?' (لمين 'whose? / for whom?').

examples.trans: Who left this envelope here?
Whose is this brown leather notebook?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنزل, بينزل).

examples.trans: Let us bring the suitcase down into the light.
Let me lower my glasses from my forehead!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of نصف ('half'); used for half hours (السبعة ونص seven thirty) and quantities (نص كاسة half a glass).

examples.trans: Breakfast starts at seven thirty.

examples.text: بس نص كاسة عصير لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Just half a glass of juice, please.

meanings.note: Singular نظارة means one pair of glasses in Arabic (نظارتي my glasses); dual نظارتين means two pairs of glasses!

examples.trans: I cannot find my glasses on the desk!
He pulled his glasses down off his forehead and laughed.

meanings.note: Contrasts with ليل ('nighttime'): بنور النهار = 'in broad daylight'.

examples.text: الشيش الأخضر طالع أحلى بكتير بنور النهار!
examples.trans: The green shutters look even lovelier in daylight!

examples.text: شتغلنا طول النهار وبالمسا شربنا شاي بالنعنع.
examples.trans: We worked all day long and in the evening had mint tea.

meanings.note: Appears in صباح النور ('morning of light', the standard reply to صباح الخير) and نور الشمس ('sunlight').

examples.trans: Good morning and welcome!
We read the card in the sunlight.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of وراء ('behind, past').

examples.trans: Look in the mirror behind the desk.
The hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أيام.

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
